svg.text: K9c ENCLOSURE — a Gastro table, liners and sliding glass instead of a custom box
Bought furniture forms the cell; a household door lock and two relays form the safety chain.
Gastro table €190 · back liner + HPL €150 · panels + track €130 · lock + reed €30
safety: lock + 2 relays ≈ €70 (K9b: €640 guard lock + €210 relay)
FRONT VIEW of the cell, built up part by part
SAFETY CHAIN: no motion while a panel is open
SPLASH ZONE at the back wall (side section)
X Y Z roll T S

g.text: panel shut → bolt in → reed closed → relays pull in
open request: relays drop first, the hand stops
then the bolt releases and the panel slides

svg.text: EN 60335 household level instead of machinery practice — risk K4, to be assessed
HPL above the splash zone (edges sealed)
z 1450: end of the splash zone
bent gutter drains to the sink
table top 1–1.2 mm on a stiffener frame
risk K8: deck flat to ±1 mm?

g.text: 1/6 A bought Gastro stainless work table (≈ 1700 × 600, €190) is the deck and the under-deck frame
2/6 A 40 × 40 aluminium profile frame carries the ceiling panel and the X box of the gantry
3/6 Stainless liners only where it splashes (to z 1450), cheap HPL panels above
4/6 An IKEA wall carcass with a stainless tray becomes the tool cabinet; IKEA fronts close the under-deck
5/6 Two sliding glazed panels close the front; a washing-machine door lock and a reed contact enable the motors
6/6 To open: the relays cut motor power first, then the lock releases and panel B slides behind panel A
